proposals.evidence: The catvāri subsection gives the MIA cayāri/cāri development, Assamese sāri, Bengali cār, Oriya cāri, Hindi cār, Old Marwari cyāri and Gujarati cār; the addendum gives Kotgarhi/Koci ċār. These eastern and western survey forms fit that r-retaining cār/cyār series, with regional affricate/sibilant outcomes. Classifier-bearing responses are excluded. The specific neuter-plural subsection is used rather than the article head.

proposals.evidence: Platts explicitly records mard and the expanded variant marad for man, male and husband, identifying the Persian origin. The existing Hindi/Urdu mard node provides the regional donor; Hajong morot and related survey variants retain the r-d/t sequence with vowel adaptation. The immediate Hindi/Urdu route is provisional for each survey locality; no direct link to a remote Sanskrit cognate is asserted.
